title: MonoPanel
description: Hosting platform for Discord bots, Node.js apps, full-stack websites, Lavalink nodes and VPSes. One panel for the storefront, billing and admin, plus a lightweight daemon on every node.

features.title: Bot & App Hosting
features.description: Give every customer an isolated server with its own RAM, CPU, disk and swap limits.
features.longDescription: Customers create servers from the software you offer (Node.js, Python, a static site, Minecraft Paper out of the box). Each server runs in its own container on a node with RAM, CPU, swap, disk and process limits, and can be started, stopped, restarted or killed from the dashboard. Bot hosting is one of five hosting types you can sell.

features.title: Hosting Types
features.description: Choose what you sell: bots, VPS, websites, Node.js or Lavalink. Anything off disappears everywhere.
features.longDescription: Under Admin > Hosting Types you tick which of the five hosting types your host provides. Whatever you leave off is removed from the home page, pricing, navigation, checkout, the customer panel, the admin menu and the API, and the server enforces it too. The change is live for every visitor with no rebuild and no restart. Set the starting selection with MONOPANEL_HOSTINGS in .env; once an admin saves a selection, that choice wins.

features.title: Website Hosting
features.description: Full-stack sites with a free subdomain, custom domains, HTTPS and Git deploys.
features.longDescription: Customers deploy a front end and back end together (Next.js, Nuxt, Express, Vite, Flask or a static site) from Git or by upload, with a build step before every start. Each site gets a free subdomain, and customers can add custom domains that the panel verifies with a TXT record or a CNAME. The daemon has a built-in reverse proxy that routes by Host header, supports websockets, serves HTTPS from certbot-style certificates and only serves domains the panel told it about.

features.title: Node.js Hosting
features.description: Any Node.js app, API or worker, with Node 20, 22, 24 or 25 and install and build tasks.
features.longDescription: Customers pick their Node.js version (20, 22, 24 or 25), deploy from Git or upload files, and run fixed install, build, pull-latest and clean tasks from the panel. The package manager follows the lockfile (npm, pnpm, yarn or bun). The panel reads package.json to show the framework, scripts and dependencies, and the live console shows the output. Customers can only run those named tasks through this route, never their own commands.

features.title: Lavalink Hosting
features.description: Lavalink v4 audio nodes for music bots, with a generated config, plugins and live stats.
features.longDescription: A Lavalink server is ready in about a minute. The panel generates application.yml from a validated settings form (sources, filters, buffers, logging) and keeps the password and port as placeholders, so changing either only needs a restart. Customers add plugins by coordinates, or switch to raw mode and edit the file themselves. The Lavalink tab shows live players, memory and CPU, and gives copy-and-paste connection details for the bot.

features.title: Live Console
features.description: Stream server output in the browser and send commands without leaving the panel.
features.longDescription: The console streams the server log through the panel as server-sent events, so the browser never talks to the node directly and node addresses and secrets stay private. Commands are sent through the panel too, and the console is rate limited per user.

features.title: File Manager
features.description: Browse, edit, upload, move, archive and extract files in the browser, with a recycle bin.
features.longDescription: Edit text files in place, upload and download files, create folders, rename, move, copy, compress and extract archives, pull a file from a URL straight onto the server, and download several items at once. Deleted files go to a recycle bin first and can be restored.

features.title: Nodes
features.description: One daemon per machine, for every hosting type. Add a node in the panel, run one command on it, done.
features.longDescription: Add a node under Admin, then run the command the panel shows on the machine. The panel talks to every daemon over HMAC-signed HTTP. A node can be limited to some hosting types (for example a Lavalink-only node), and website nodes get their own DNS target. You can test a node, reconcile it, rotate its secret, hide it from new deployments and move servers between nodes.

features.title: VPS Hosting
features.description: Sell VPSes with root access, SSH and a choice of Ubuntu or Debian.
features.longDescription: Every VPS is a Docker container with sshd, Docker, Node.js, pm2 and build tools. Customers pick Ubuntu 22.04, Ubuntu 24.04 or Debian 12, and can power, resize, reset the root password, run commands and browse files from the panel. Running Docker inside a VPS works safely with the Sysbox runtime.

features.title: Billing & Credits
features.description: Credits, orders and coupons. Manual payments are verified by staff, and cards go through Stripe Checkout.
features.longDescription: Customers pay by UPI, bank transfer, crypto, gift card or, once you enable it, by card through Stripe Checkout. Manual payments sit in a queue until staff verify them, and Stripe payments are only credited after Stripe's signed webhook arrives. Coupons, orders and pending approvals are all managed from the admin panel.

features.title: Support & Mail
features.description: A ticket desk and an in-dashboard inbox, built in.
features.longDescription: Customers open and follow support tickets. Staff can message one customer or broadcast to everyone through the Mail Center, customers get an inbox with an unread counter, and admins see read receipts for every message sent.

features.title: Team Access
features.description: Invite people to a server and grant only the permissions they need.
features.longDescription: Owners can share a server with other accounts and pick from ten permissions: reading the console, sending commands, power actions, reading and writing files, backups, schedules, addons, SFTP and settings. Team access follows the owner's plan.

features.title: Backups
features.description: Create, download and restore server backups, limited by the slots a plan gives.
features.longDescription: The daemon archives a server's files and the panel tracks the backup slots each plan includes. Backups can be downloaded and restored, and a schedule can create them automatically.

features.title: Scheduled Tasks
features.description: Run console commands, power actions and backups on a cron schedule.
features.longDescription: A schedule holds one to six tasks run in order with an optional delay between them. The plan is checked when a schedule is created and every time it fires, so a lapsed plan simply pauses automation.

features.title: SFTP Access
features.description: Built-in SFTP server with one login per server and no shell access.
features.longDescription: Enable SFTP on a node and customers log in with their panel username and server id, using a password they create in the server's settings. A login only ever sees that one server's files, symlinks are not followed, writes respect the disk quota, and shell and exec are refused.

features.title: Addons & Store
features.description: Sell or give away plugins and templates that install onto a server in one click.
features.longDescription: Admins define addons as files to download onto a server, with the software they work with. Customers install them from their server page, pay in coins or credits, and are refunded automatically if the node fails the install. A coin store also sells upgrades such as extra RAM, CPU and disk.

features.title: REST API & Webhooks
features.description: Scoped API keys and signed webhooks for your own tooling.
features.longDescription: Admins create API keys with scopes, optional IP allow-lists and expiry dates, and can revoke or rotate them at any time. Webhooks are delivered with an HMAC-SHA256 signature and refuse to call private addresses.

requirements: Node.js 22.13 or newer for the panel, Node.js 20 or newer for the daemon
PostgreSQL 12 or newer (the panel and every daemon each need their own database)
A Docker, Podman or bubblewrap setup on nodes that run servers (bots, Node.js, websites, Lavalink)
Docker on nodes that host VPSes
Ports 80 and 443 on nodes that host websites (or your own front proxy such as Caddy or nginx)
tar and unzip on nodes (backups and archive extraction)

panelSteps.title: Configure
commands: # set DATABASE_URL, APP_URL, ALLOWED_ORIGINS and JWT_SECRET in .env

daemonSteps.title: Add the node in the panel
commands: # Admin > Nodes (servers) and/or Admin > VPS Nodes (VPSes). The panel shows the exact command to run, with your values filled in.

daemonSteps.title: Get the code, build, configure and start
commands: cd /opt/monopanel-daemon && npm install && npm run build
# optional: --services nodejs,lavalink limits what this node accepts
